tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
tools.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

schema.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__computer
schema.description: Mouse/keyboard automation in the Browser pane. Clicks accept either `coordinate` (pixels in the coordinate frame of the most recent `computer{action:"screenshot"}` — reported with every scaled screenshot; equal to the image's pixels for unscaled ones) or `ref` (a `ref_N` from read_page/find). Whenever you intend to click on an element like an icon, you should consult a screenshot to determine the coordinates of the element first; after the tab loads a different site, take a new screenshot before clicking by `coordinate`.

tabId.description: Tab to act on within the preview context. Omit for the fronted tab; get ids from tabs_context.

action.description:
The action to perform:
* `left_click`: Click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `right_click`: Click the right mouse button at the specified coordinates to open context menus.
* `double_click`: Double-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `triple_click`: Triple-click the left mouse button at the specified coordinates.
* `type`: Type a string of text.
* `screenshot`: Take a screenshot of the screen.
* `wait`: Wait for a specified number of seconds.
* `scroll`: Scroll up, down, left, or right at the specified coordinates.
* `key`: Press a specific keyboard key.
* `left_click_drag`: Drag from start_coordinate to coordinate.
* `zoom`: Take a screenshot of a specific region for closer inspection.
* `scroll_to`: Scroll an element into view using its element reference ID from read_page or find tools.
* `hover`: Move the mouse cursor to the specified coordinates or element without clicking. Useful for revealing tooltips, dropdown menus, or triggering hover states.

coordinate.description: (x, y): The x (pixels from the left edge) and y (pixels from the top edge) coordinates. Required for `left_click`, `right_click`, `double_click`, `triple_click`, and `scroll`. For `left_click_drag`, this is the end position.

text.description: The text to type (for `type` action) or the key(s) to press (for `key` action). For `key` action: Provide space-separated keys (e.g., "Backspace Backspace Delete"). Supports keyboard shortcuts using the platform's modifier key (use "cmd" on Mac, "ctrl" on Windows/Linux, e.g., "cmd+a" or "ctrl+a" for select all). Page zoom shortcuts (e.g. "cmd+=", "ctrl+-", "cmd+0") are not supported - use the `zoom` action to magnify a region of the page instead.

duration.description: The number of seconds to wait. Required for `wait`. Maximum 10 seconds.

scroll_direction.description: The direction to scroll. Required for `scroll`.

scroll_amount.description: The number of scroll wheel ticks. Optional for `scroll`, defaults to 3.

region.description: (x0, y0, x1, y1): The rectangular region to capture for `zoom`. Coordinates define a rectangle from top-left (x0, y0) to bottom-right (x1, y1) in pixels from the viewport origin. Required for `zoom` action. Useful for inspecting small UI elements like icons, buttons, or text.

scale.description: For `screenshot` and `zoom` only. Scale factor in [0.1, 1] for the returned image; 1 (default) uses the full image token budget, 0.5 returns an image at half the width and height (~quarter of the tokens). Coordinates are ALWAYS in the full-resolution coordinate frame (reported with every scaled screenshot), never in the scaled image's own pixels.

repeat.description: Number of times to repeat the key sequence. Only applicable for `key` action. Must be a positive integer between 1 and 100. Default is 1. Useful for navigation tasks like pressing arrow keys multiple times.

ref.description: Element reference ID from read_page or find tools (e.g., "ref_1", "ref_2"). Required for `scroll_to` action. Can be used as alternative to `coordinate` for click actions.

modifiers.description: Modifier keys for click actions. Supports: "ctrl", "shift", "alt", "cmd" (or "meta"), "win" (or "windows"). Can be combined with "+" (e.g., "ctrl+shift", "cmd+alt"). Optional.

action_summary.description: A few words saying what this action does on the page and to what, for example 'Sends the drafted reply to pat@example.com' or 'Opens the Filters menu'. Set it on every left_click, right_click, double_click, triple_click, left_click_drag, key and type action. State the effect only, and accurately: no reasons, nothing about what you were asked or allowed to do, no passwords or other secrets.

tools.name: mcp__Claude_Browser__resize_window
tools.description: Emulate a viewport size in the Browser pane tab. Presets: mobile (375x812), tablet (768x1024), or desktop, which clears the size emulation and returns the tab to the pane's own responsive size. Custom sizes need both width and height. An emulated size applies to that tab across reloads and navigation (scaled down to fit when it is larger than the pane): reset it with preset "desktop" as soon as you finish testing. The desktop app may also clear a size you set when your turn ends, so set it again in a later turn if you still need it. A size the user picked from the pane's own Viewport menu is theirs and stays until they or you change it; leave it unless they ask. colorScheme (light/dark) emulates prefers-color-scheme on that tab; it survives reloads and preset "desktop" does not touch it, but the pane re-syncs the tab to the app's light/dark theme when that theme changes or the pane reopens; local documents and static HTML previews always render light. The mobile preset (and any width < 768) also emulates a mobile device: Android Chrome user agent and 5 touch points, so pages detect a touch phone; your clicks still arrive as mouse clicks. Reload the page after switching so load-time device gates re-run.

action.description: What to do. theorem newArena_clause6 {s : S3} {st i : Nat} (hk : KInv s) (h : NewArenaBase s st i) :
    WF3 s ∧ I1 s ∧ AnchorOrder s ∧ AnchorOrderHeld s ∧
      ArenaInv s ⟨st, i, footprint s.P st, []⟩ :=
  ⟨hk.1, hk.2.1.1.1, hk.2.1.2.1, hk.2.2.1, (newEntry_inv h).1⟩

/-- `newArena` without the guard preserves the library invariant (§55, §76). -/
theorem lInv_newArena {L : LState} {st i : Nat} (h : NewArenaBase L.kern st i) (hi : LInv L) :
    LInv (newArenaEff L st i) := by
  intro F hF
  rcases List.mem_append.1 hF with hF | hF
  · exact hi F hF
  · rw [List.mem_singleton.1 hF]
    have hia := h.internalAuth
    cases hy : L.kern.A[i]? with
    | none => rw [hy] at hia; exact hia.elim
    | some y => exact ⟨lt_of_getElem? hy, fun _ => newEntry_inv h⟩

/-- `issue` preserves the library invariant, for the issuing entry and every other entry (§55,
§77). -/
theorem lInv_issue {k : K} {L L' : LState} {i : Nat} {region : List Nat} {dst : Nat}
    (hs : IssueD k i region dst L (.ok L')) (hi : LInv L) : LInv L' := by
  cases hs with
  | @ok E s₁ s₂ hE hst hav hsp hsto =>
  obtain ⟨hp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsp
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hsto
  rw [← issueKEff_eq]
  have hEm : E ∈ L.arenas := List.mem_of_getElem? hE
  have hright : IssueRight L.kern E region := fun l hl => by
    rw [hp.modifyOn region (List.mem_singleton_self _) l hl]; exact allows_some_modify _
  have hil := (hi E hEm).1
  have hAe : (issueKEff L.kern E region dst).A =
      L.kern.A ++ [⟨.modify, some E.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩] := rfl
  have hold : ∀ F ∈ L.arenas, F.internal < (issueKEff L.kern E region dst).A.length ∧
      (Live (issueKEff L.kern E region dst) F → EntryInv (issueKEff L.kern E region dst) F) := by
    intro F hF
    obtain ⟨hlt, hinv⟩ := hi F hF
    refine ⟨by rw [hAe, List.length_append]; omega, fun hl => ?_⟩
    exact entryInv_append (hinv ((akeep_append hAe).active_back hl hlt)) hAe rfl rfl rfl hl
  intro F hF
  rcases List.mem_or_eq_of_mem_set hF with hF | rfl
  · exact hold F hF
  · obtain ⟨hlt, hinv'⟩ := hold E hEm
    refine ⟨hlt, fun hl => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨hai, hsh⟩ := hinv' hl
    obtain ⟨hai0, hsh0⟩ := (hi E hEm).2 hst.live
    have hnew : (issueKEff L.kern E region dst).A[L.kern.A.length]? =
        some ⟨.modify, some E.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩ := by simp [hAe]
    have hold' : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, e.2 < L.kern.A.length := fun e he => by
      obtain ⟨y, hy, -⟩ := hsh0 e he; exact lt_of_getElem? hy
    have hact : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, (issueKEff L.kern E region dst).Active e.2 → L.kern.Active e.2 :=
      fun e he ha => (akeep_append hAe).active_back ha (hold' e he)
    -- an active issued block and the new region are disjoint (§43, case 3; §77.5)
    have hdis : ∀ e ∈ E.issued, L.kern.Active e.2 → ∀ l ∈ region, l ∉ e.1 := by
      intro e he ha l hl hle
      obtain ⟨y, hy, -, -, hf, hm⟩ := hsh0 e he
      obtain ⟨y', hy', ya⟩ := ha
      rw [hy] at hy'; cases hy'
      exact effective_ne_modify_of_desc hy ya (hf ▸ hle) (hai0.derived e he ⟨y, hy, ya⟩) hm
        (allows_modify_iff.1 (hright l hl))
    refine ⟨⟨hai.storageUsable, hai.fpEq, hai.active, hai.shape,
      fun l hl => hai.availableIn l (List.mem_filter.1 hl).1, fun e he l hl => ?_,
      fun e he e' he' hne ha ha' l hl hl' => ?_, fun e he ha l hl hla => ?_,
      fun e he ha => ?_⟩, fun e he => ?_⟩
    · rcases List.mem_cons.1 he with rfl | he
      · exact hst.regionIn l hl
      · exact hai.issuedIn e he l hl
    · rcases List.mem_cons.1 he with rfl | he <;> rcases List.mem_cons.1 he' with rfl | he'
      · exact hne rfl
      · exact hdis e' he' (hact e' he' ha') l hl hl'
      · exact hdis e he (hact e he ha) l hl' hl
      · exact hai.disjoint e he e' he' hne ha ha' l hl hl'
    · have hla' := List.mem_filter.1 hla
      rcases List.mem_cons.1 he with rfl | he
      · simp at hla'; exact hla'.2 hl
      · exact hai.notAvailable e he ha l hl hla'.1
    · rcases List.mem_cons.1 he with rfl | he
      · show E.internal ∈ (L.kern.addAuth ⟨.modify, some E.internal, region, .place dst, true⟩).ancs
          L.kern.A.length
        rw [ancs_addAuth_self rfl hil]; exact List.mem_cons_self ..
      · exact hai.derived e he ha
    · rcases List.mem_cons.1 he with rfl | he
      · exact ⟨_, hnew, rfl, hil, rfl, rfl⟩
      · exact hsh e he

/-- `reset` preserves the library invariant, for the reset entry and every other entry (§55,
§78). -/
theorem lInv_reset {L L' : LState} {i : Nat} (hs : ResetD i L (.ok L')) (hi : LInv L) :
    LInv L' := by
  cases hs with
  | @ok E s₁ s₂ hE hd hrl _ =>
  obtain ⟨hdp, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hd
  obtain ⟨-, rfl⟩ := Guarded.ok_iff.1 hrl
  rw [← resetKEff_eq]
  have hEm : E ∈ L.arenas := List.mem_of_getElem? hE
  have hAe : (resetKEff L.kern E).A = L.kern.A ++
      [⟨.modify, some E.internal, footprint L.kern.P E.storage, .frame L.kern.top, false⟩] := rfl
  have hold : ∀ F ∈ L.arenas, F.internal < (resetKEff L.kern E).A.length ∧
      (Live (resetKEff L.kern E) F → EntryInv (resetKEff L.kern E) F) := by
    intro F hF
    obtain ⟨hlt, hinv⟩ := hi F hF
    refine ⟨by rw [hAe, List.length_append]; omega, fun hl => ?_⟩
    exact entryInv_append (hinv ((akeep_append hAe).active_back hl hlt)) hAe rfl rfl rfl hl
  intro F hF
  rcases List.mem_or_eq_of_mem_set hF with hF | rfl
  · exact hold F hF
  · obtain ⟨hlt, hinv'⟩ := hold E hEm
    refine ⟨hlt, fun hl => ?_⟩
    obtain ⟨hai, -⟩ := hinv' hl
    exact ⟨⟨hai.storageUsable, hai.fpEq, hai.active, hai.shape, fun l hl => hl,
      fun _ he => (by cases he), fun _ he => (by cases he), fun _ he => (by cases he),
      fun _ he => (by cases he)⟩, fun _ he => (by cases he)⟩

/-- A kernel step of non-administrative code preserves the library invariant (§55), when the
state before satisfies `WF3` and the state after `NoDangling` (§57): the storage of a live arena
stays usable since `internal` covers it. -/
theorem lInv_kernel {k : K} {L : LState} {s' : S3} (hk : KStep k L.kern s') (hw : WF3 L.kern)
    (hnd : NoDangling s') (hi : LInv L) : LInv ⟨s', L.arenas⟩ := by
  have hA := kstep_akeep hk
  intro E hE
  obtain ⟨hlt, hinv⟩ := hi E hE
  refine ⟨hA.lt hlt, fun hlive => ?_⟩
  have hEI := hinv (hA.active_back hlive hlt)
  have hfp := kstep_fp hk hEI.1.storageUsable.lt
  refine entryInv_transport hEI hA hfp ?_ hlive
  obtain ⟨l, hl⟩ := exists_mem_footprint hw (L.kern.P.length - E.storage + 1) E.storage (by omega)
    hEI.1.storageUsable.lt
  obtain ⟨yi, hyi, -⟩ := hEI.1.active
  obtain ⟨y', hy', -, hf', -⟩ := hA _ yi hyi
  obtain ⟨y'', hy'', ya''⟩ := hlive
  rw [hy'] at hy''; cases hy''
  have hli : l ∈ yi.footprint := by
    have := (hEI.1.fpEq l).2 hl; simpa [S3.afp, hyi] using this
  exact usable_of_covered hnd hy' ya'' (hf' ▸ hli) ((hfp l).2 hl)

/-- Every library step, with or without the guard of §56, preserves the library invariant (§55),
when the kernel state before satisfies `WF3` and the one after `NoDangling` (§57). -/
theorem lInv_stepNG {k : K} {L L' : LState} (h : LStepNG k L L') (hw : WF3 L.kern)
    (hnd : NoDangling L'.kern) (hi : LInv L) : LInv L' := by
  cases h with
  | kernel hk => exact lInv_kernel hk hw hnd hi
  | newArena hb => exact lInv_newArena hb hi
  | issue hs => exact lInv_issue hs hi
  | reset hs => exact lInv_reset hs hi

/-- Conditional `ArenaInv` (§55) on library runs with or without the guard of §56: every live
entry of a reachable library state satisfies `EntryInv`, **provided** every kernel-reachable state
satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling` (`hK`). `hK` is part of the main-invariant claim of §57, which is
false as stated (`Access.reachable_kinv_false`, the §63 ownership cycle). At `(K0, st)`, the
instance of every witness of this file, both `hK` (`Witness.lReach_inv_hyp_false`) and the
conclusion (`Witness.lReach_inv_conclusion_false`, `Witness.arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`) are
false. This theorem is therefore a conditional, not a proof that `ArenaInv` is preserved on
library runs. Only `lInv_newArena`, `lInv_issue` and `lInv_reset` hold with no kernel
hypothesis; `lInv_kernel` and `lInv_stepNG` take the per-step instances of `hK` (`WF3` before,
`NoDangling` after), which the breaking `transfer` of `Witness.arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`
violates. -/
theorem lReachNG_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (hK : ∀ s, Reachable k statics s → WF3 s ∧ NoDangling s) {L : LState}
    (h : LReachNG k statics L) : LInv L := by
  induction h with
  | init => intro E hE; cases hE
  | step hL hs ih => exact lInv_stepNG hs (hK _ hL.reachable).1 (hK _ (hL.step hs).reachable).2 ih

/-- Conditional `ArenaInv` (§55) on library-reachable states: every live entry satisfies
`ArenaInv`, **provided** every kernel-reachable state satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling` (`hK`, part
of the §57 claim, false as stated: `Access.reachable_kinv_false`). At `(K0, st)` both `hK` and
the conclusion are false (`Witness.lReach_inv_hyp_false`, `Witness.lReach_inv_conclusion_false`):
an accepted `transfer` (§63) makes the storage of a live arena unusable
(`Witness.arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`). A conditional only (see `lReachNG_inv`). -/
theorem lReach_inv {k : K} {statics : Statics}
    (hK : ∀ s, Reachable k statics s → WF3 s ∧ NoDangling s) {L : LState}
    (h : LReach k statics L) : ∀ E ∈ L.arenas, Live L.kern E → ArenaInv L.kern E :=
  fun E hE hl => ((lReachNG_inv hK h.ng E hE).2 hl).1

/-! ## Safe reuse after `reset` (§78, §86) -/

/-- Library steps keep the authorities (§42, §58, Part XIV). -/
theorem lstep_akeep {k : K} {L L' : LState} (h : LStep k L L') : AKeep L.kern L'.kern := by
  cases h with

(.issue (i := 0) (region := [1]) (dst := 2)
      (.ok (E := rE') (by decide) (by decide) (by decide) (.ok (by decide)) (.ok (by decide))))
  have hk := KInvB.sound (s := r8.kern) (by decide)
  exact ⟨h8, hk.1, hk.2, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide, by decide,
    by decide, .ok (by decide)⟩

/-! ### `ArenaInv` broken by an accepted `transfer` (§55, §57, §63)

A run from the same initial state in which the storage of a live arena is the destination of an
accepted `transfer` that closes an ownership cycle (§63 `ok` effect), the recorded §63 defect
(`Access.reachable_kinv_false`). -/

/-- `alloc(0, 0, [leaf])`: place 3, owned by the static place 0, root authority 3 (§71). -/
def t1 : S3 := allocEff (S3.init st) 0 [(none, 0)]
/-- `alloc(0, 3, [leaf])`: place 4, owned by place 3, root authority 4 (§71). -/
def t2 : S3 := allocEff t1 3 [(none, 0)]
/-- `alloc(0, 3, [leaf])`: place 5, owned by place 3, root authority 5 (§71). -/
def t3 : S3 := allocEff t2 3 [(none, 0)]
/-- `derive(4, [4], Modify)`: authority 6 on the leaf of place 4, held by frame 0 (§60). -/
def t4 : S3 := deriveEff t3 4 [4] .modify
/-- `store(6, 5)`: authority 6 becomes `internal`, held by the arena value 5 (§65). -/
def t5 : LState := ⟨storeEff t4 6 5, []⟩
/-- `newArena(4, 6)`: storage 4, `internal` 6, arena value 5 (§76). -/
def t6 : LState := newArenaEff t5 4 6
/-- `transfer(0, 4)`: the value of place 0 moves into the storage 4; place 3, owned by 0, becomes
owned by 4, itself owned by 3 (§63 `ok` effect). -/
def t7 : LState := ⟨transferEff t6.kern 0 4, t6.arenas⟩
/-- The entry registered by `newArena(4, 6)` (§46, §76). -/
def tE : ArenaEntry := ⟨4, 6, [4], []⟩

/-- **`ArenaInv` fails on a library-reachable state** (spec problem; §55 item 1, §57, §63). From a
library-reachable state satisfying `KInv ∧ KAux`, whose only entry is live with usable storage 4,
`transfer(0, 4)` is accepted (§63) and closes the ownership cycle 3 ↔ 4. The entry stays live
(`internal` 6 is active, §46), but its storage is no longer usable: §55 item 1 ("`storage`
designates an existing, usable place") fails. No library step of the run is outside Part XIV. -/
theorem arenaInv_broken_by_transfer :
    LReach K0 st t7 ∧ KInv t6.kern ∧ KAux t6.kern ∧ t6.arenas = [tE] ∧ t6.kern.Usable 4 ∧
    TransferStep K0 0 4 t6.kern (.ok t7.kern) ∧ t7.arenas = [tE] ∧ Live t7.kern tE ∧
    ¬ t7.kern.Usable tE.storage ∧ ¬ ArenaInv t7.kern tE := by
  have h1 : LReach K0 st ⟨t1, []⟩ := .step .init
    (.kernel (KStep.alloc (pr := 0) (ow := 0) (ls := [(none, 0)])
      (AllocStep.ok (by decide) trivial)))
  have h2 : LReach K0 st ⟨t2, []⟩ := .step h1
    (.kernel (KStep.alloc (pr := 0) (ow := 3) (ls := [(none, 0)])
      (AllocStep.ok (by decide) trivial)))
  have h3 : LReach K0 st ⟨t3, []⟩ := .step h2
    (.kernel (KStep.alloc (pr := 0) (ow := 3) (ls := [(none, 0)])
      (AllocStep.ok (by decide) trivial)))
  have h4 : LReach K0 st ⟨t4, []⟩ := .step h3 (.kernel (.derive (.ok (by decide))))
  have h5 : LReach K0 st t5 := .step h4 (.kernel (.store (.ok (by decide))))
  have h6 : LReach K0 st t6 := .step h5 (.newArena (others := []) (.ok (by decide)))
  have ht : TransferStep K0 0 4 t6.kern (.ok t7.kern) := .ok (by decide)
  have hk := KInvB.sound (s := t6.kern) (by decide)
  have hu : ¬ t7.kern.Usable tE.storage := by decide
  exact ⟨.step h6 (.kernel (.transfer ht)), hk.1, hk.2, by decide, by decide, ht, by decide,
    by decide, hu, fun h => hu h.storageUsable⟩

/-- The conclusion of `lReach_inv` is false at `(K0, st)` (§55, §63): some live entry of a
library-reachable state does not satisfy `ArenaInv` (`arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`). -/
theorem lReach_inv_conclusion_false :
    ¬ ∀ L, LReach K0 st L → ∀ E ∈ L.arenas, Live L.kern E → ArenaInv L.kern E := fun h =>
  let ⟨hr, _, _, _, _, _, ha, hl, _, hn⟩ := arenaInv_broken_by_transfer
  hn (h t7 hr tE (by rw [ha]; exact List.mem_singleton_self _) hl)

/-- The hypothesis of `lReach_inv` and `lReachNG_inv` is false at `(K0, st)` (§57 as stated,
§63): some kernel-reachable state violates `WF3` or `NoDangling`; otherwise `lReach_inv` would
contradict `lReach_inv_conclusion_false`. -/
theorem lReach_inv_hyp_false : ¬ ∀ s, Reachable K0 st s → WF3 s ∧ NoDangling s :=
  fun hK => lReach_inv_conclusion_false fun _ h => lReach_inv hK h

/-! ### `newArena` accepted where §76.6 fails (§76.6, §49.8, §55, §63)
616:/-- `NoDangling` (§54): a place containing a leaf covered by an active authority is usable. -/
617:theorem usable_of_covered {s : S3} (hnd : NoDangling s) {j q l : Nat} {y : Authority}

1619:    (hnd : NoDangling s') (hi : LInv L) : LInv ⟨s', L.arenas⟩ := by
1638:when the kernel state before satisfies `WF3` and the one after `NoDangling` (§57). -/

1649:satisfies `WF3` and `NoDangling` (`hK`). `hK` is part of the main-invariant claim of §57, which is
1656:`NoDangling` after), which the breaking `transfer` of `Witness.arenaInv_broken_by_transfer`
1659:    (hK : ∀ s, Reachable k statics s → WF3 s ∧ NoDangling s) {L : LState}

# Reading policy for the reference kernel (fixed by the orchestrator; every item is reported for arbitration)

General
- The frozen spec specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md is the only semantic source. Cite clauses as §N or §N.k (item k).
- Formalize each clause as written. Never add a clause the text does not state (no "robustness"); never drop one.
- When a clause has no checkable content in the state (undefined term), do not invent content: omit it from the definition and record it in readings.md (clause, quote, why it cannot be formalized).
- When a clause has two readings, use the one listed below; if the case is not listed, use the draft's reading if the draft matches one of the readings, and record it in readings.md with both readings and an example of a program whose verdict changes.
- A representation choice that changes no accepted program is free (record it briefly).

State (§38): S3 = (F, nF, P, I, A, D, dead, pin). No arena registry, no callParams, no freed. Library state lives elsewhere.
Outcomes (§58): one type Outcome3 σ := ok σ | reject | fail; every O1–O16 relation except alloc never yields fail.
O1 derive (§60): takes a region (List Nat, read extensionally), not a place. Preconditions: active source; ExercisableAt source mode; every leaf of region exists, is a leaf, belongs to afp source; mode ≤ effective mode of source on each leaf; §60.3 as a decidable clause (no unrelated active authority becomes incompatible); §60.4 current frame live. §60.1c "origin chain and anchors valid" and §60.4b "footprint and anchoring restrictions": no checkable content -> omitted, recorded.
O2 split (§61): draft clauses (incl. no exclusive right already distributed). §61.4 is NOT a precondition (the §61 note says an accepted split may violate I1 without DDSound) -> recorded.
O3 release (§62): draft clauses; §62.5 (abstraction contracts) omitted, recorded.
O4 transfer (§63): draft clauses MINUS the draft's extra clause "(transferEff s src dst).Usable dst" (not in §63); PLUS §63.8 (local self-blocking prevention, as LockOptions.Opt2Transfer on formal/derivability_0.1); effect: dependencies follow the corresponding places corr(r) (not all to the destination root); §63.6 over moved usable places and AnchorOrder in the resulting state; §63.7 AnchorOrderHeld for the moved held authorities in the resulting state; §63.4 = draft ActiveDerivedOutside reading (recorded); §63.2 child order = place index order (recorded).
O5 depend (§64): draft clauses; §64.2b "real dependency" omitted, recorded.
O8 store (§65): draft clauses (they match).
O9/O10/O11 (§66–§68): add "every leaf belongs to a usable place" (§66.1, §67.1, §68.1); O10 keeps §67.2 explicitly.
O12 endUse (§69): death markers transitive over owned storage; drop the draft's extra disjunct that blocks descendants of authorities the step releases (not in §69.2) -> record the consequence.
O13 free (§70): death markers transitive; no extra "Usable p" and no clearing of D beyond what §70 prescribes; §70.4 scope = the released unit (place and storage that dies with it).
O14 alloc (§71): shape nonempty with exactly ONE root (one new storage root), parts' parents inside the shape, no owner component; provider clause as written in §71.2 (Modify OR writeShared over SharedMutable metadata) -> conflict with §36 recorded; outcomes reject / fail (not Satisfiable) / ok.
O6 enterFrame (§72): locals owned directly by the new frame (no local owned by another local); §72.3 ParamOriginHidden; §72.4 AnchorOrderHeld in the resulting state.
O7 exitFrame (§73): draft (first surviving active origin, held by a frame or a usable place).
O15/O16 pin/unpin (§74, §75): per-leaf dynamic pin flags (draft); unpin requires the place usable and K.ExternalDone(place) on the place; StaticPinnedBottom is a condition on (K, statics), not on states.
HasRight / ExercisableAt (§43): one authority exercisable at m with sufficient effective mode on every leaf (∃ a, ∀ l) as the draft -> recorded.
WF3 (§49): a structure with eight named fields, one per item:
 1 frames: F nonempty, no duplicates, every frame < nF;
 2 places: parent links valid and acyclic (representation: parent index < child index), parts share the owner and death marker of their parent;
 3 owners: owner frames < nF, owner places exist; "well-founded ownership chains reaching a live frame for every usable place" read as stated for usable places (Usable is inductive) -> recorded with the global-acyclicity alternative;
 4 footprints: every footprint member is an existing leaf;
 5 authorities: origins exist and precede (origin index < id: representation of acyclic chains ending at a root);
 6 RootChain (draft);
 7 RootHeld as §49.7 states it: every usable root place has an active root authority, Modify, no origin, held by its owner, whose footprint is the place's footprint (draft RootLive + mode);
 8 holder validity (draft poss).
 The draft's converse RootHeld (every origin-less authority covering a leaf of root r is held by r's owner) is NOT a WF3 clause: keep it as a separate auxiliary predicate.
I2 (§51): mode conservation unconditional (not under ∀ p ∈ footprint).
Initial state (§47): base frame 0; statics may be owned by statics; root authority held by the owner. Well-formedness of the statics declaration (acyclic ownership, parents before children) is not stated by §47: keep the draft ShapeOK-style hypothesis as a hypothesis of the init theorems and record it as a spec gap.
Reachable: closure of S3.init statics under the kernel steps O1–O16 only.

diff --git a/formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean b/formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean
index 40bc6e7..6e5bc10 100644
--- a/formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean
+++ b/formal/Ern/Lib/HandlePool.lean
@@ -2052,11 +2052,148 @@ theorem free_slot_init :
   exact ⟨_, .step (.step w3_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 h₁)
     (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 h₂, rfl, by decide⟩
 
+/-! ### The kernel state reached by `freeSlot` (§36, §57, §69, §89; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3)
+
+From `w4`, a frame derives from `internal` over slot place 1, writes it and releases the derived
+authority; `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` then ends the slot content. The kernel run `k1`–`k5` is the same
+run without the write of slot place 1. -/
+
+/-- After `derive(3, [1], Modify)` from `internal` (§60): authority 4 over slot place 1. -/
+def v1 : PState := { w4 with kern := deriveEff w4.kern 3 [1] .modify }
+
+/-- After `write` of slot place 1 through authority 4 (§67): the slot content is `Init`. -/
+def v2 : PState := { v1 with kern := write3Eff v1.kern [1] }
+
+/-- After the kernel `release(4)` (§62). -/
+def v3 : PState := { v2 with kern := releaseEff v2.kern 4 }
+
+/-- `v3` is reached by a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57, §60,
+§62, §67; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1, D.3). -/
+theorem v3_reach : PReachI K0 hst v3 := by
+  have h1 : PReachI K0 hst v1 := .step w4_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+  have h2 : PReachI K0 hst v2 := .step h1 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.kernel (.write (a := 4) (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+  exact .step h2 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.kernel (.release (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+
+/-- Kernel run, step 1: `derive(0, [1, 2], Modify)` from `S3.init hst` (§47, §60). -/
+def k1 : S3 := deriveEff (S3.init hst) 0 [1, 2] .modify
+
+/-- Kernel run, step 2: `store(3, 3)` (§65). -/
+def k2 : S3 := storeEff k1 3 3
+
+/-- Kernel run, step 3: `write` of place 4 (§67), the kernel side of the `allocSlot` of `w4`. -/
+def k3 : S3 := write3Eff k2 [4]
+
+/-- Kernel run, step 4: `derive(3, [1], Modify)` (§60). -/
+def k4 : S3 := deriveEff k3 3 [1] .modify
+
+/-- Kernel run, step 5: `release(4)` (§62). -/
+def k5 : S3 := releaseEff k4 4
+
+/-- `k5` is reached from `S3.init hst` by kernel steps O1–O16 alone (§57, §60, §62, §65, §67). -/
+theorem k5_reach : Reachable K0 hst k5 :=
+  .step (.step (.step (.step (.step .init (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+    (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide)))) (.write (a := 2) (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+    (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide)))) (.release (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
+
+/-- The kernel state of `w4` is `k3` (§57; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1, D.3). -/
+theorem k3_eq : k3 = w4.kern := rfl
+
+/-- Kernel states with equal components are equal (§38). -/
+theorem s3_ext {s t : S3} (hF : s.F = t.F) (hn : s.nF = t.nF) (hP : s.P = t.P)
+    (hI : ∀ l, s.I l = t.I l) (hA : s.A = t.A) (hD : ∀ q, s.D q = t.D q)

+  subst hF hn hP hA
+  have e1 : _ := funext hI
+  have e2 : _ := funext hD
+  have e3 : _ := funext hd
+  have e4 : _ := funext hp

+
+A third run, from `PState.init Witness.est` under `Examples.K0` (§47, §48), in which no client
+kernel step (`PStep.kernel`) has a companion as source. Pool 1 is nested in slot 0 of pool 0: its
+`internal` is derived from the entry authority of a resolution of pool 0, which D.4 permits ("Les
+dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau"). -/
+
+/-- Statics of the entry-route witnesses (§47; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): place 0 is the storage
+of pool 0, with children 1 and 2 (its slots); place 1 has two leaf children 3 and 4 (the slots of
+pool 1); places 0 to 4 are `Uninit`; place 5 is the value of pool 0 (`Init`); place 6 will hold the
+`internal` of pool 1; places 7 and 8 are handle destinations. Root authorities 0 to 4 cover places
+0, 5, 6, 7 and 8. -/
+def est : Statics :=
+  [((none, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false),
+    ((some 1, none, 0), false), ((some 1, none, 0), false),
+    ((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false), ((none, none, 0), false),
+    ((none, none, 0), false)]
+
+/-- Initial library state of the entry-route witnesses (§47). -/
+def e0 : PState := PState.init est
+
+/-- After `derive(0, footprint of place 0, Modify)` (§60): authority 5, the `internal` of pool 0. -/
+def e1 : PState := { e0 with kern := deriveEff e0.kern 0 (footprint e0.kern.P 0) .modify }
+
+/-- After `store(5, 5)` (§65): the `internal` of pool 0 is held by place 5. -/
+def e2 : PState := { e1 with kern := storeEff e1.kern 5 5 }
+
+/-- After `newPool(0, 5)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): pool 0 over storage 0, slots 1 and 2 free,
+of generation 0 (§47). -/
+def e3 : PState := newPoolEff e2 0 5
+
+/-- Pool 0 of the entry-route run after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §47). -/
+def peA : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 5, [⟨1, 0, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩
+
+/-- After `allocSlot(0, 7)` on slot 0 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the handle `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is
+written into place 7 (§67). -/
+def e4 : PState := allocSlotEff e3 0 peA 0 ⟨1, 0, false⟩ 7
+
+/-- Pool 0 of the entry-route run after `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §47). -/
+def peA4 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 5, [⟨1, 0, true⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩
+
+/-- After `resolve(0, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, Modify)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2): the `Modify` companion 6
+of pool 0 over the storage, and the entry authority 7 over slot place 1, that is, leaves 3 and 4

+    [(e4.kern.A.length + 1, 0, 0)]⟩] }

+/-- After `store(8, 6)` (§65): the `internal` of pool 1 is held by place 6. -/

+/-- After `allocSlot(1, 8)` on slot 0 of pool 1 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the handle

+/-- `e9` is reached by a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv`; its client

+/-- Shape of `e9` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2, D.4): the resolution of pool 0, with companion 6 and
+entry authority 7, is recorded; the origin of the `internal` 8 of pool 1 is the entry authority 7,
+not a companion; 6, 7 and 8 are active, and `KInv` holds (§42, §57). -/
+theorem e9_shape :
+    (⟨0, 5, 6, .modify, [(7, 0, 0)]⟩ : Res) ∈ e9.res ∧ e9.kern.org 8 = some 7 ∧
+    e9.kern.Active 6 ∧ e9.kern.Active 7 ∧ e9.kern.Active 8 ∧ KInv e9.kern :=

+    PReachI K0 est e9 ∧ KInv e9.kern ∧ ¬ FreeGuarantee K0 e9 ∧ ¬ PoolInv K0 e9 := by
+  have hG : ¬ FreeGuarantee K0 e9 := fun hG =>

+/-- Contract problem (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles
+compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool"), without client access to a companion: on `e9`,

+theorem entry_resolve_modify_exclusive_false :
+    ∃ L', ResolveStep 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ .modify e9 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 est L' ∧

+    .ok (pl := peB9) (sl := ⟨3, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)

+
+/-! ### Nested pools through an entry authority over the whole storage (HandlePool v0.4 annex,

+
+A fourth run, from `PState.init Witness.gst` under `Examples.K0` (§47, §48). Pool 0 has a single
+slot whose place covers its whole storage, so the entry authority of its resolution covers that
+storage. The `internal` of pool 1 is derived from that entry authority; no client kernel step has a

+
+/-- Statics of the whole-storage entry-route witnesses (§47; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): place 0 is
+the storage of pool 0, with one child 1 (its only slot); place 1 has two leaf children 2 and 3 (the
+slots of pool 1); places 0 to 3 are `Uninit`; place 4 is the value of pool 0 (`Init`); place 5 will

+def gst : Statics :=
+  [((none, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false),
+    ((some 1, none, 0), false), ((some 1, none, 0), false),
+    ((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false), ((none, none, 0), false),
+    ((none, none, 0), false)]
+
+/-- Initial library state of the whole-storage entry-route witnesses (§47). -/
+def g0 : PState := PState.init gst
+
+/-- After `derive(0, footprint of place 0, Modify)` (§60): authority 5, the `internal` of pool 0. -/
+def g1 : PState := { g0 with kern := deriveEff g0.kern 0 (footprint g0.kern.P 0) .modify }
+
+/-- After `store(5, 4)` (§65): the `internal` of pool 0 is held by place 4. -/
+def g2 : PState := { g1 with kern := storeEff g1.kern 5 4 }
+
+/-- After `newPool(0, 5)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): pool 0 over storage 0, with the single free
+slot 1, of generation 0 (§47). -/
+def g3 : PState := newPoolEff g2 0 5
+
+/-- Pool 0 of the whole-storage run after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §47). -/
+def pgA : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 5, [⟨1, 0, false⟩]⟩
+
+/-- After `allocSlot(0, 6)` on slot 0 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the handle `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is
+written into place 6 (§67). -/

+
+/-- Pool 0 of the whole-storage run after `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §47). -/
+def pgA4 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 5, [⟨1, 0, true⟩]⟩
+
+/-- After `resolve(0, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩, Modify)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2): the `Modify` companion 6
+of pool 0 over the storage, and the entry authority 7 over slot place 1, which covers the whole
+storage (§60). -/
+def g5 : PState := { g4 with
+  kern := deriveEff (compS g4.kern pgA4 .modify) g4.kern.A.length (footprint g4.kern.P 1) .modify
+  res := g4.res ++ [⟨pgA4.id, pgA4.internal, g4.kern.A.length, .modify,

+/-- After `derive(7, [2, 3], Modify)` from the entry authority 7 (§60; HandlePool v0.4 annex,
+D.4): authority 8, the `internal` of pool 1. -/
+def g6 : PState := { g5 with kern := deriveEff g5.kern 7 [2, 3] .modify }
+
+/-- After `store(8, 5)` (§65): the `internal` of pool 1 is held by place 5. -/
+def g7 : PState := { g6 with kern := storeEff g6.kern 8 5 }
+
+/-- After `newPool(1, 8)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): pool 1 over storage place 1, the content of
+the only slot of pool 0 (§47, §56). -/
+def g8 : PState := newPoolEff g7 1 8
+
+/-- Pool 1 of the whole-storage run after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §47). -/
+def pgB : Pool := ⟨1, 1, 8, [⟨2, 0, false⟩, ⟨3, 0, false⟩]⟩
+
+/-- After `allocSlot(1, 7)` on slot 0 of pool 1 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the handle
+`⟨1, 0, 0⟩` is written into place 7 (§67). -/
+def g9 : PState := allocSlotEff g8 1 pgB 0 ⟨2, 0, false⟩ 7
+
+/-- Pool 1 of the whole-storage run after `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §47). -/
+def pgB9 : Pool := ⟨1, 1, 8, [⟨2, 0, true⟩, ⟨3, 0, false⟩]⟩
+
+/-- `g9` is reached by a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv`; its client
+kernel steps derive from authorities 0 and 7 only (§57, §60, §65, §67; HandlePool v0.4 annex,
+D.1–D.4). -/
+theorem g9_reach : PReachI K0 gst g9 := by
+  have h1 : PReachI K0 gst g1 := .step .init (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+  have h2 : PReachI K0 gst g2 := .step h1 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+  have h3 : PReachI K0 gst g3 := .step h2 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
+  have h4 : PReachI K0 gst g4 := .step h3 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.allocSlot (.ok (pl := pgA) rfl (by decide) rfl rfl))
+  have r5 : ResolveStep 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ .modify g4 (.ok g5) :=
+    .ok (pl := pgA4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
+  have h5 : PReachI K0 gst g5 := .step h4 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolve r5)
+  have h6 : PReachI K0 gst g6 := .step h5 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+  have h7 : PReachI K0 gst g7 := .step h6 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))
+  have h8 : PReachI K0 gst g8 := .step h7 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
+  exact .step h8 (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
+    (.allocSlot (.ok (pl := pgB) rfl (by decide) rfl rfl))
+
+/-- Shape of `g9` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2, D.4): the origin of the `internal` 8 of pool 1 is the
+entry authority 7, whose origin is companion 6; the resolution of pool 0 is recorded and 6 is
+active (§42). -/
+theorem g9_shape : g9.kern.org 8 = some 7 ∧ g9.kern.org 7 = some 6 ∧
+    (⟨0, 5, 6, .modify, [(7, 0, 0)]⟩ : Res) ∈ g9.res ∧ g9.kern.Active 6 := by decide
+
+/-- Contract problem (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3 and D.4, item 3), without client access to a
+companion: `FreeGuarantee` and `PoolInv` are false on `g9` (`g9_reach`). `freeSlot(⟨1, 0, 0⟩)` of
+pool 1 is accepted on slot place 2, while the entry authority 7, an active strict descendant of
+companion 6 of pool 0, covers place 2; 7 is an ancestor of the `internal` 8 of pool 1, exempted by
+D.3 (§43, §69). -/
+theorem entry_whole_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false :
+    ¬ FreeGuarantee K0 g9 ∧ ¬ PoolInv K0 g9 := by
+  have hG : ¬ FreeGuarantee K0 g9 := fun hG =>
+    hG 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ _
+      (.ok (pl := pgB9) (sl := ⟨2, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide))
+      pgB9 ⟨2, 0, true⟩ (by decide) (by decide) ⟨0, 5, 6, .modify, [(7, 0, 0)]⟩ (by decide) 7
+      (by decide) (by decide) 2 (by decide) (by decide)
+  exact ⟨hG, fun h => hG h.2.2⟩
+
+/-- Contract problem (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles
+compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool"), without client access to a companion and in its
+whole-storage reading: on `g9`, the `Modify` companion 6 of pool 0 is active, yet
+`resolve(1, ⟨1, 0, 0⟩, Modify)` is accepted and creates the `Modify` companion 9 of pool 1, whose
+footprint is the whole storage of pool 0; the reached state violates `ModifyExclusive` while 6
+stays active (§43, §50, §60). -/
+theorem entry_whole_resolve_modify_exclusive_false :
+    ∃ L', ResolveStep 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ .modify g9 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 gst L' ∧
+      ¬ ModifyExclusive L' ∧ L'.kern.afp 9 = footprint L'.kern.P pgA4.storage ∧
+      L'.kern.Active 6 := by
+  have hok : ResolveStep 1 ⟨1, 0, 0⟩ .modify g9 (.ok _) :=
+    .ok (pl := pgB9) (sl := ⟨2, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
+  refine ⟨_, hok, .step g9_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolve hok), fun hM => ?_,
+    by decide, by decide⟩
+  exact absurd (hM ⟨0, 5, 6, .modify, [(7, 0, 0)]⟩ (by decide) ⟨1, 8, 9, .modify, [(10, 0, 0)]⟩
+    (by decide) pgA4 (by decide) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl ⟨2, by decide, by decide⟩)
+    (by decide)
+

# Annexe D — Instance `HandlePool` (non normative, contrat de bibliothèque)

Cette annexe décrit une **instance de bibliothèque** de la discipline MM-03, et non une nouvelle opération primitive du langage. Les noms sont sémantiques. Le contrat doit être reconstruit et vérifié ; les résultats du jalon 3 concernent le modèle exploratoire et ses conditions, **pas** automatiquement les règles corrigées ci-dessous.

## D.1 — Identité, état et stockage

Un handle est une donnée `(poolId, slot, gen)` **sans autorité d'accès intrinsèque**. L'identité logique `poolId` est fraîche et n'est pas réutilisée pendant l'exécution pertinente : détruire puis recréer un pool à la même adresse ne réactive pas un ancien handle. Chaque pool vivant conserve une entrée abstraite `{storage, internal, slots}`, où chaque slot possède `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`. Les slots sont des sous-emplacements deux à deux disjoints, inclus dans `storage` ; leur métadonnée abstraite est représentée en octets par l'implémentation de bibliothèque.

`storage` peut être local, statique, alloué ou être un bloc issu d'une arène. **`newPool(storage, internal)` exige que toutes les feuilles du stockage d'entrée soient `Uninit`** et doit vérifier la garde unifiée de MM-03.3 §2.7 bis sur les deux registres des abstractions vivantes. Il reprend les autres obligations applicables de `newArena` sans fabriquer ni droits ni initialisation des valeurs de slots. Les entrées libres sont `Uninit` ; leur génération initiale est zéro. Une autorité ne peut être `internal` de deux abstractions vivantes, et une arène ne peut réutiliser l'`internal` d'un pool vivant.

## D.2 — Emprunt composé et résolution

Une résolution réussie dérive **de `internal` une autorité compagne** couvrant toutes les feuilles du stockage du pool, de mode `Observe` ou `Modify`, puis dérive **de cette compagne** une autorité de même mode par entrée résolue. L'autorité d'entrée est une descendante de la compagne, et non une autre dérivation indépendante de `internal`. Les deux sont soumises aux règles ordinaires de modes effectifs, d'exercice, de détention, d'ancrage et de transfert ; aucune permission nouvelle n'est créée.

`resolve(h, Observe | Modify)` vérifie l'identité de pool, la génération et la vivacité du slot **avant toute création d'autorité** : handle d'un autre pool, périmé, slot absent ou libre ⇒ `fail`, sans changement d'état. Une résolution valide exige l'exercice légal de `internal` au mode requis. Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool ; des compagnes `Observe` peuvent coexister. Il est impossible de libérer une compagne tant que ses descendantes d'entrée sont actives (O3.2). La propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau, pas seulement deux appels successifs de `resolve`.

`resolveMany(handles, Modify)` crée **une** compagne `Modify` et une autorité `Modify` par entrée. La distinction des slots est vérifiée dynamiquement pour ce lot ; toute identité invalide, génération périmée, entrée libre ou répétition de slot donne `fail` **atomique**, sans création partielle de droits. `resolveMany(handles, Observe)` utilise des dérivations `Observe` de la compagne `Observe`, **sans `split` ni contrôle de distinction** : la répétition du même handle valide est permise. Les `reject` de discipline d'accès restent distincts des `fail` de validation des handles.

`unresolve` libère d'abord toutes les dérivées d'entrée encore actives, puis la compagne. Les règles de `release`, y compris celles qui empêchent la libération en présence de descendants ou d'ancres valides, restent applicables ; le contrat ne supprime pas silencieusement des autorités transférées.

## D.3 — Allocation et fin d'usage de slot

`allocSlot(pool, dst)` exige un pool vivant, l'autorisation d'administration de ses métadonnées, une destination utilisable et libre d'autorité active, non `Init`, apte à recevoir la représentation d'un handle. `fail` si aucun slot libre ; `ok` choisit un slot libre, le rend vivant, conserve sa génération et écrit son handle dans la seule feuille `dst`, selon les obligations de représentation (Spec 4) et d'ABI (Spec 11). **Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit`** jusqu'à son écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot.

`freeSlot(h)` exige un pool **vivant** et `MetaRight`, c'est-à-dire le droit légal d'administration de la valeur pool par `Modify` exerçable ou par mutation `writeShared` admissible de ses métadonnées `SharedMutable`. `fail` si l'identité ou la génération ne correspond pas ; un slot déjà libre n'est pas rendu libérable par cette seule égalité. Pour réussir, la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible : **aucune dépendance utilisable** ne serait invalidée, **aucune feuille n'est épinglée**, et **aucune autorité active ne couvre l'entrée hors `internal` et ses ancêtres**. En particulier, aucune descendante active d'une compagne ne doit subsister sur cette entrée. Le contrôle n'interprète pas `internal` comme un emprunt externe empêchant systématiquement le nettoyage de ses propres slots.

L'effet `ok` applique au **contenu** les effets de fin d'usage d'`endUse`, remet les feuilles de l'entrée à `Uninit`, marque l'entrée libre et incrémente sa génération ; **il ne désalloue pas implicitement l'allocation MM-02 du stockage**. Il ne s'agit pas de supposer une invocation de O12 autorisée par simple `MetaRight` : la correspondance des effets et la préservation des invariants sous ce droit constituent une **obligation explicite de reconstruction**, notamment dans les cas `writeShared`.

## D.4 — Invariant corrigé et limites

`PoolInv` exige : (1) les entrées sont deux à deux disjointes et incluses dans le stockage ; (2) aucune autorité d'entrée active ne désigne un slot libre ou une ancienne génération (`pool_no_stale_access`) ; (3) **garantie de transition** : `freeSlot` n'aboutit jamais si une descendante active d'une compagne couvre le slot concerné. La dernière clause concerne le succès des transitions, non une interdiction globale de toutes les dérivations du noyau sur des slots libres. Les dérivations ordinaires issues d'une autorité d'entrée restent permises par le noyau.

Les générations sont des entiers naturels dans le modèle abstrait. Leur débordement ou leur recyclage dans une représentation finie doivent être empêchés par l'implémentation (par exemple retrait définitif d'un slot) ; l'ABI est spécifiée en Spec 11. L'encapsulation qui empêche un client d'accéder directement à une compagne administrative appartient à la Spec 9. Les handles persistants peuvent représenter des liens cycliques ; les résolutions qui en découlent restent temporaires et soumises à MM-03.

**Statut des preuves :** le jalon 3 rapporte `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, `pool_no_stale_access`, `pool_resolveMany_atomic`, `pool_resolveMany_distinct`, `pool_freeSlot_ends_content` et `pool_entries_disjoint` sur son brouillon, sous les hypothèses détaillées dans `J3_v0.1.md`. Il rapporte également un contre-exemple à l'ancienne formulation de `pool_inv_preserved`. **Il ne constitue pas encore la preuve** de la nouvelle règle `freeSlot` sous `MetaRight` ni de la totalité du contrat corrigé : ces obligations sont consignées en annexe F.

# Annexe E — Registre inter-spécifications (non normatif pour la Spec 1)

| Destination | Obligations ouvertes ou précisées |
|---|---|
| **Spec 2 — Concurrence** | Partie concurrente de `stat` ; `writeShared` et synchronisation ; transférabilité, partageabilité, suspension concurrente ; cas H39, H41. |
| **Spec 3 — Contrôle de flux et appels** | Protection forte de paramètres (`Reach`, `lineage`, `derivedIn`, G1', A3 strict) ; ré-emprunt d'un paramètre `Modify` par un paramètre dérivé `Observe` (H01, admis dans le noyau séquentiel, sans promettre la protection forte) ; **passage par valeur (`sink`) vers l'appelé** : prévoir la primitive MM-03 correspondante, transfert d'un emplacement de l'appelant vers un local de l'appelé au moment de l'entrée, sans affaiblir arbitrairement O4 ; retour et `defer` (H16, H27b, H38, H40, H42). |
| **Spec 4 — Types** | Validité de représentation (`dec`), `SameSizeAlong`, information de forme pour des régions non contiguës, feuille de destination d'une référence typée, correspondance `kind` et type ; **mémoire rendue par une abstraction de réutilisation (bloc d'arène réémis, entrée de pool) exposée comme typée non initialisée jusqu'à écriture explicite**, sans réinterprétation implicite d'anciens octets. La décision ne change pas rétroactivement les effets d'initialisation de `reset` sur l'état abstrait MM-03. |
| **Spec 9 — Encapsulation** | Empêcher l'usage extérieur des autorités internes/compagnes administratives des bibliothèques sûres. |
| **Spec 11 — ABI** | Alignement (`dec`), taille/encodage et décodage des références et handles, largeur des adresses, espace fini et épuisement, générations bornées, placement et jetons (`PlacementOK`, `TokCompat`). |
| **Spec 13 — Compilateur** | Justification du lowering de `noalias` au-delà de l'exclusivité du noyau. |
| **Spécification des ressources** | Obligations de libération attachées à certains types (H43). |
| **Bibliothèques** | `DeclaredDisjoint` par disjonction réelle des feuilles ; `FreeCompat`, représentation et atomicité des métadonnées d'arène/pool, garantie unifiée des registres `internal`, contrat `MetaRight` et fin de slot. |

import Ern.MemoryModel.Arena
import Ern.MemoryModel.Access.Preserve.EndFree

/-!
# Handle pool: a library instance of the access discipline (non-normative)

**Non-normative.** This module formalizes the library contract "HandlePool v0.4 annex" (items
D.1–D.4), which `specs/ERN_Memory_Model_Specification_v0.md` does not define (§75, Part XIV
preamble: "The contracts of `HandlePool` and `DataStack` belong to their library abstractions and
are not defined here"). The normative clauses that constrain it are
§36 (`MetaRight` is exercisable `Modify` on the administering value; `writeShared` alone is
insufficient), §37 and §89 (handles are data, not authorities), §38 and §46 (library state outside
`S₃`), §47 (empty initial registry), §56 (the guard over all registries of live administrations)
and §58 (outcomes, statics before `fail`).

The pool registry lives beside the kernel state (`PState`). Its operations are built on the
kernel operations O1–O16 (§60–§75): `newPool` registers only; `allocSlot` writes the handle into
its destination (O10); `resolve` derives a companion from `internal` over the whole storage, then
an entry authority from the companion (O1 twice); `resolveMany` does the same with `split` (O2) in
`Modify` and with one `Observe` derive per handle (O1) in `Observe`; `unresolve` releases (O3).
`freeSlot` applies the effect function of O12 (§69) to the slot content under preconditions that
exempt `internal` and its ancestors (`ContentEndPre`): it is not a kernel `endUse` step.
`contentEnd_preserves` proves that it preserves `KInv ∧ KAux` (§57); `pstep_kernel` states what
every pool step is on the kernel side.
-/

namespace Ern.Lib.HandlePool

open Ern.MemoryModel
open Ern.MemoryModel.Access

/-! ## Library state (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §38, §46) -/

/-- Slot of a pool entry (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: `{place, gen : Nat, live : Bool}`;
non-normative library contract; §38, §46). -/
structure Slot where
  place : Nat
  gen : Nat
  live : Bool
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Pool entry `{storage, internal, slots}` with its logical identity (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1;
non-normative library contract). The pool value is the place holding `internal` (§46 analogue). -/
structure Pool where
  id : Nat
  storage : Nat
  internal : Nat
  slots : List Slot
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Handle `(poolId, slot, gen)`: data, not an authority (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §37, §89;
non-normative library contract). -/
structure Handle where
  id : Nat
  slot : Nat
  gen : Nat
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Ghost record of a resolution (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2; auxiliary information creating no
right, §38): pool identity and `internal`, the companion, the mode, and the entry authorities
tagged with their slot and resolved generation. Read only by `unresolve` and by the invariants. -/
structure Res where
  pool : Nat
  internal : Nat
  comp : Nat
  mode : Mode
  entries : List (Nat × Nat × Nat)
deriving DecidableEq, Repr

/-- Library state (§38, §46; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library contract): the
kernel state `S₃` and, separately, the pool registry, the next fresh pool identity and the ghost
resolutions. -/
structure PState where
  kern : S3
  pools : List Pool
  nId : Nat
  res : List Res

/-- Initial library state (§47; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): the initial kernel state, an empty
registry. -/
def PState.init (statics : Statics) : PState := ⟨S3.init statics, [], 0, []⟩

/-- The pool read as an arena entry with nothing available or issued, to reuse `MetaRight` of §36
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract). -/
def Pool.entry (pl : Pool) : Arena.ArenaEntry := ⟨pl.storage, pl.internal, [], []⟩

/-- Administrative right on the pool (§36; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36;
non-normative library contract): the pool is live (`internal` active) and `MetaRight` holds,
exercisable `Modify` over the pool value; no `writeShared` branch. -/
def AdminRight (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Prop := s.Active pl.internal ∧ Arena.MetaRight s pl.entry

/-- Decidability of `AdminRight` (§36). -/
instance (s : S3) (pl : Pool) : Decidable (AdminRight s pl) := by
  unfold AdminRight; infer_instance

/-- Place of slot `i`, `0` if absent (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; non-normative library
contract; §46). -/
def slotPlace (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) : Nat := ((pl.slots[i]?).map (·.place)).getD 0

/-- The pool with slot `i` replaced (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library

def Exempt (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Prop := x = i ∨ x ∈ s.ancs i

/-- Decidability of `Exempt` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
instance (s : S3) (i x : Nat) : Decidable (Exempt s i x) := by unfold Exempt; infer_instance

/-- §69.2 for storage that dies with the content (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: the end-of-use
effects of O12; non-normative library contract): an active derived authority over a leaf of a place
that stops being usable is held within the slot `q` or by a dying holder. -/
def DyingAccessOK (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[j]?) (fun y => y.active = true → y.origin ≠ none →
    (∃ l ∈ y.footprint, isLeaf s.P l ∧ s.Usable l ∧ ¬ (endUseS s q).Usable l) →
      heldIn s.P q y.holder ∨ ¬ HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `DyingAccessOK` (§69.2). -/
instance (s : S3) (q j : Nat) : Decidable (DyingAccessOK s q j) := by
  unfold DyingAccessOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- §69.3 with the exemption of D.3 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library contract):
anchor `x` of a place remaining usable is not held within the slot `q` and keeps a live holder;
unless exempt, it is not a root of `q`. -/
def ContentAnchorOK (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Prop :=
  OptP (s.A[x]?) (fun y => ¬ heldIn s.P q y.holder ∧ (¬ Exempt s i x → ¬ IsRootOf s q y) ∧
    HolderLive (endUseS s q) y.holder) True

/-- Decidability of `ContentAnchorOK` (§69.3). -/
instance (s : S3) (q i x : Nat) : Decidable (ContentAnchorOK s q i x) := by
  unfold ContentAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of the end of the content of slot place `q` of the pool of `internal` `i`
(HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "la fin logique du contenu doit être admissible"; the preconditions
of O12, §69, excluding `internal` and its ancestors; non-normative library contract). §69.1 is not
a precondition: `freeSlot_modify_right` derives it from `AdminRight`. -/
structure ContentEndPre (k : K) (s : S3) (q i : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- D.3: no active authority covers the entry except `internal` and its ancestors (§69.2 on the
  leaves of the entry, with the exemption). -/
  entry : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j → (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) →
    Exempt s i j
  /-- §69.2 on the storage that dies with the content. -/
  dying : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j
  /-- D.3, §69.3: no usable dependency is invalidated. -/
  anchors : ∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
    ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x
  /-- D.3, §69.4: no ending leaf is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l

/-- Decidability of `ContentEndPre` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §69). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (q i : Nat) :
    Decidable (ContentEndPre k s q i) :=
  decidable_of_iff ((∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, s.Active j →
      (∃ l ∈ s.afp j, l ∈ footprint s.P q) → Exempt s i j) ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, DyingAccessOK s q j) ∧
    (∀ q' ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s q).Usable q' →
      ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s q).D q', ContentAnchorOK s q i x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s q l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d⟩⟩

/-- Effect of `freeSlot` on slot `i` of pool `j` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; non-normative library
contract): the effects of O12 on the slot content (`endUseEff`, §69), no deallocation; the slot
becomes free and its generation is incremented. -/
def freeSlotEff (L : PState) (j : Nat) (pl : Pool) (i : Nat) (sl : Slot) : PState :=
  { L with
    kern := endUseEff L.kern sl.place
    pools := L.pools.set j (setSlot pl i ⟨sl.place, sl.gen + 1, false⟩) }

/-- `freeSlot(h)` on pool `j` as a relation (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3, corrected by §36; §58;
non-normative library contract): `reject` without the pool, without a live pool or `MetaRight`;
then `fail` for a handle of another pool, stale, absent or free; then `reject` unless the end of
the content is admissible (`ContentEndPre`). -/
inductive FreeSlotStep (k : K) (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L : PState) : Outcome3 PState → Prop where
  | noPool : L.pools[j]? = none → FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | noRight {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → ¬ AdminRight L.kern pl →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | fail {pl : Pool} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl → ¬ HandleOK pl h →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .fail
  | noEnd {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ¬ ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L .reject
  | ok {pl : Pool} {sl : Slot} : L.pools[j]? = some pl → AdminRight L.kern pl →
      HandleOK pl h → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl → ContentEndPre k L.kern sl.place pl.internal →
      FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok (freeSlotEff L j pl h.slot sl))

/-! ## Library runs (HandlePool v0.4 annex; §38, §46, §57) -/

/-- One `ok` step of a library run (HandlePool v0.4 annex; non-normative library contract): a
kernel step O1–O16 of non-administrative code, the registry unchanged, or an accepted pool
operation (§57, §58). -/
inductive PStep (k : K) : PState → PState → Prop where
  | kernel {L : PState} {s' : S3} : KStep k L.kern s' → PStep k L { L with kern := s' }
  | newPool {L L' : PState} {others : List (List Nat)} {st i : Nat} :
      NewPoolStep others st i L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | allocSlot {L L' : PState} {j dst : Nat} : AllocSlotStep j dst L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolve {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveStep j h m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | resolveMany {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {hs : List Handle} {m : Mode} :
      ResolveManyStep k j hs m L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | unresolve {L L' : PState} {c : Nat} : UnresolveStep c L (.ok L') → PStep k L L'
  | freeSlot {L L' : PState} {j : Nat} {h : Handle} : FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
      PStep k L L'

/-- Library states reachable from the initial library state (§47) by library steps (HandlePool v0.4
annex; non-normative library contract). -/
inductive PReach (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReach k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReach k statics L → PStep k L L' → PReach k statics L'

/-- Library runs in which every step starts from a kernel state satisfying `KInv` (§57; HandlePool
v0.4 annex). Under the guarantee of §57 every library-reachable state is such a state
(`PReach.toI`); the pool theorems are stated on these runs, so that they do not depend on that
guarantee. -/
inductive PReachI (k : K) (statics : Statics) : PState → Prop where
  | init : PReachI k statics (PState.init statics)
  | step {L L' : PState} : PReachI k statics L → KInv L.kern → PStep k L L' →
      PReachI k statics L'

open Examples

/-- Statics of the witnesses (§47; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
def hst : Statics :=
  [((none, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false), ((some 0, none, 0), false),
    ((none, none, 0), true), ((none, none, 0), false)]

/-- Initial library state (§47). -/
def w0 : PState := PState.init hst

/-- After `derive(0, [1, 2], Modify)` (§60): authority 3, the future `internal`. -/
def w1 : PState := { w0 with kern := deriveEff w0.kern 0 [1, 2] .modify }

/-- After `store(3, 3)` (§65): `internal` is held by the pool value, place 3. -/
def w2 : PState := { w1 with kern := storeEff w1.kern 3 3 }

/-- After `newPool(0, 3)` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1): pool 0 with slots 1 and 2, free, of
generation 0 (§47). -/
def w3 : PState := newPoolEff w2 0 3

/-- Pool 0 after `newPool` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1; §47). -/
def pl3 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 3, [⟨1, 0, false⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩

/-- After `allocSlot(0, 4)` on slot 0 (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3): the handle `⟨0, 0, 0⟩` is
written into place 4 (§47, §67). -/
def w4 : PState := allocSlotEff w3 0 pl3 0 ⟨1, 0, false⟩ 4

/-- Pool 0 after `allocSlot` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §47). -/
def pl4 : Pool := ⟨0, 0, 3, [⟨1, 0, true⟩, ⟨2, 0, false⟩]⟩

/-- `w3` is reached by a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57, §60,
§65; HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1). -/
theorem w3_reach : PReachI K0 hst w3 :=
  .step (.step (.step .init (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.kernel (.store (Guarded.ok (by decide))))) (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.newPool (others := []) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))

/-- `w4` is library-reachable (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3; §47, §67). -/
theorem w4_reach : PReachI K0 hst w4 :=
  .step w3_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1
    (.allocSlot (.ok (pl := pl3) rfl (by decide) rfl rfl))

/-- `resolveMany` in `Observe` accepts a repeated valid handle (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "la
répétition du même handle valide est permise"): two `Observe` entry authorities on slot 0, derived
from one `Observe` companion; the same batch in `Modify` fails (§60). -/
theorem observe_repeat_ok :
    (∃ L', ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .observe w4 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      L'.res = [⟨0, 3, 4, .observe, [(5, 0, 0), (6, 0, 0)]⟩]) ∧
    ∀ o, ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .modify w4 o → o = .fail := by
  have hok : ResolveManyStep K0 0 [⟨0, 0, 0⟩, ⟨0, 0, 0⟩] .observe w4 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) rfl (by decide) (by decide) (by decide)
  exact ⟨⟨_, hok, .step w4_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.resolveMany hok), rfl⟩,
    (pool_resolveMany_distinct (L' := w4) (pl := pl4)).1 rfl (by decide) (by decide)⟩

/-- `freeSlot` is not a kernel `endUse` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "Le contrôle n'interprète pas
`internal` comme un emprunt externe"; §69.2): on `w4`, `freeSlot(⟨0, 0, 0⟩)` is accepted, while the
kernel `endUse` of slot place 1 is rejected, because `internal` (authority 3, derived, active,
covering place 1) is held by the pool value outside the slot. Both states satisfy `KInv ∧ KAux`
(§57), decided through `Arena.KInvB`. -/
theorem freeSlot_not_endUse :
    (∃ L', FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ w4 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      KInv L'.kern ∧ KAux L'.kern) ∧
      ¬ EndUsePre K0 w4.kern 1 ∧ KInv w4.kern ∧ KAux w4.kern := by
  have hok : FreeSlotStep K0 0 ⟨0, 0, 0⟩ w4 (.ok _) :=
    .ok (pl := pl4) (sl := ⟨1, 0, true⟩) rfl (by decide) (by decide) rfl (by decide)
  have hk4 : KInv w4.kern ∧ KAux w4.kern := Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)
  exact ⟨⟨_, hok, .step w4_reach hk4.1 (.freeSlot hok), Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)⟩, by decide,
    hk4⟩

/-- Contract problem (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.3: "Le contenu du slot demeure `Uninit` jusqu'à son
écriture ; l'écriture du handle dans `dst` n'initialise pas le slot"): the preconditions of
`allocSlot` do not exclude a destination inside the allocated slot. On `w3`, `allocSlot(0, 1)` is
accepted on slot 0, whose place is 1: the slot becomes live and its content `Init` (§67). -/
theorem allocSlot_into_own_slot :
    ∃ L', AllocSlotStep 0 1 w3 (.ok L') ∧ PReachI K0 hst L' ∧
      L'.pools[0]? = some pl4 ∧ L'.kern.I 1 = .init := by
  have hok : AllocSlotStep 0 1 w3 (.ok (allocSlotEff w3 0 pl3 0 ⟨1, 0, false⟩ 1)) :=
    .ok rfl (by decide) rfl rfl
  exact ⟨_, hok, .step w3_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 (.allocSlot hok), rfl, by decide⟩

/-- Contract problem (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.1: "Les entrées libres sont `Uninit`"): free
entries are not `Uninit` in every library-reachable state. On `w3`, a frame with `Modify` over the
pool value derives from `internal` over slot place 1 (O1, §60) and writes it (O10, §67): slot 0
stays free while its content is `Init`. -/
theorem free_slot_init :
    ∃ L, PReachI K0 hst L ∧ L.pools[0]? = some pl3 ∧ L.kern.I 1 = .init := by
  have h₁ : PStep K0 w3 { w3 with kern := deriveEff w3.kern 3 [1] .modify } :=
    .kernel (.derive (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
  have h₂ : PStep K0 { w3 with kern := deriveEff w3.kern 3 [1] .modify }
      { w3 with kern := write3Eff (deriveEff w3.kern 3 [1] .modify) [1] } :=
    .kernel (.write (a := 4) (Guarded.ok (by decide)))
  exact ⟨_, .step (.step w3_reach (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 h₁)
    (Arena.KInvB.sound (by decide)).1 h₂, rfl, by decide⟩

instance (s : S3) (p x : Nat) : Decidable (EndUseAnchorOK s p x) := by
  unfold EndUseAnchorOK OptP; split <;> infer_instance

/-- Preconditions of `endUse` (§69). -/
structure EndUsePre (k : K) (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Prop where
  /-- §69.1: `place` is usable. -/
  usable : s.Usable p
  /-- §69.1: exercisable `Modify` over `place`. -/
  right : HasRight s .modify p
  /-- §69.2: no active derived authority over an ending leaf is held outside the dying places. -/
  access : ∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, EndUseAccessOK s p j
  /-- §69.3: no place usable after the effect depends on an authority held by `place`, its root,
  or an authority whose holder dies. -/
  anchors : ∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q →
    ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q, EndUseAnchorOK s p x
  /-- §69.4: no ending leaf, owned storage included, is pinned, statically or dynamically. -/
  notPinned : ∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l

/-- Decidability of the preconditions of `endUse` (§69). -/
instance (k : K) [DecidablePred k.Pinned] (s : S3) (p : Nat) : Decidable (EndUsePre k s p) :=
  decidable_of_iff (s.Usable p ∧ HasRight s .modify p ∧
    (∀ j ∈ List.range s.A.length, EndUseAccessOK s p j) ∧
    (∀ q ∈ List.range s.P.length, (endUseS s p).Usable q →
      ∀ x ∈ (endUseS s p).D q, EndUseAnchorOK s p x) ∧
    (∀ l ∈ List.range s.P.length, EndingLeaf s p l → s.pin l = false ∧ ¬ k.Pinned l))
    ⟨fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩, fun ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩ => ⟨a, b, c, d, e⟩⟩

/-- `endUse` as a relation (§69). -/
def EndUseStep (k : K) (p : Nat) (s : S3) : Outcome3 S3 → Prop :=
  Guarded (EndUsePre k s p) (endUseEff s p)

/-! ## O13 `free` (§70) -/

  | .place _ => true

435:For every administrative abstraction, including arenas, `HandlePool`, and `DataStack`, **`MetaRight` requires `Modify` exercisable on the administering value**. The `writeShared` branch alone is insufficient. Operations issuing, recycling, ending, or invalidating regions must preserve active authorities and dependencies. Allocation through administration shared among simultaneous holders, under an interface not providing such exclusive exercise, cannot be expressed in safe code with only these sequential operations: any synchronized implementation of it belongs to Spec 2. These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel.
1043:In a generation-based pool library abstraction, a handle may contain a logical pool identity, an entry identifier, and a generation. This handle is not, by itself, an access right. Safe resolution temporarily supplies authority when the pool and entry are valid; a stale identity or generation leads to defined failure. These conditions belong to the safe abstraction's contract and do not modify the authority-discipline kernel.

def FreeGuarantee (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →

/-- Same-pool restriction of the transition guarantee (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3;
non-normative library contract). This is not the contract's statement (`FreeGuarantee`): only the
companions of the slot's pool are quantified (`r.pool = pl.id`). On that point it is weaker; it also
covers the companion itself, and on that point it is stronger (§43, §69). -/
def FreeGuaranteeSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ (j : Nat) (h : Handle) (L' : PState), FreeSlotStep k j h L (.ok L') →
    ∀ (pl : Pool) (sl : Slot), L.pools[j]? = some pl → pl.slots[h.slot]? = some sl →
      ∀ r ∈ L.res, r.pool = pl.id → ∀ x, L.kern.Active x → (x = r.comp ∨ r.comp ∈ L.kern.ancs x) →
        ∀ l ∈ L.kern.afp x, l ∉ footprint L.kern.P sl.place

/-- `PoolInv` as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, as corrected; non-normative
library contract): entry disjointness, `pool_no_stale_access`, and the transition guarantee of
`freeSlot` (§55, §57). It is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
def PoolInv (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop := EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuarantee k L

/-- Same-pool restriction of `PoolInv` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4; non-normative library
contract): items 1 and 2 as the contract states them, item 3 restricted to the companions of the
slot's pool (`FreeGuaranteeSamePool`). This is not the contract's statement (`PoolInv`) (§55,
§57). -/
def PoolInvSamePool (k : K) (L : PState) : Prop :=
  EntriesDisjoint L ∧ NoStale L ∧ FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L

/-- `EntriesDisjoint` follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1)
(§40). -/
theorem entriesDisjoint_of {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) : EntriesDisjoint L := by
  intro pl hpl
  have hok := hwf.pools _ (List.mem_map_of_mem hpl)
  exact ⟨fun sl hsl l hl => hok.slotIn sl.place (List.mem_map_of_mem (f := (·.place)) hsl) l hl,
    fun a b sa sb ha hb hab => hok.disjoint a b sa.place sb.place
      (by simp [Pool.shape, ha]) (by simp [Pool.shape, hb]) hab⟩

/-- The same-pool transition guarantee follows from the ghost well-formedness (HandlePool v0.4
annex, D.4, item 3, restricted to the slot's pool): an active descendant of a companion of the pool
is younger than `internal`, so it is neither `internal` nor one of its ancestors, and
`ContentEndPre` forbids it to cover the entry (§43, §69). -/
theorem freeGuaranteeSamePool_of {k : K} {L : PState} (hwf : PoolWF L) :
    FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L := by
  intro j h L' hst pl sl hpj hsl r hr hrp x hx hxr l hl hlq
  cases hst with
  | @ok pl' sl' hpj' _ _ hsl' hpre =>
    rw [hpj] at hpj'; cases hpj'
    rw [hsl] at hsl'; cases hsl'
    obtain ⟨hint, hlt, -, -⟩ := res_internal hwf hr (List.mem_of_getElem? hpj) hrp
    obtain ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ := hx
    have hex := hpre.entry x (List.mem_range.2 (lt_of_getElem? hy)) ⟨y, hy, ya⟩ ⟨l, hl, hlq⟩
    have hcx : r.comp ≤ x := by
      rcases hxr with rfl | hc
      · exact Nat.le_refl _
      · exact Nat.le_of_lt (chain_lt hc)
    unfold Exempt at hex
    rcases hex with rfl | h'
    · omega
    · have := chain_lt h'; omega

/-- `pool_inv_preserved`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4): `PoolInvSamePool`
holds on every state of a library run whose steps start from states satisfying `KInv` (§57); with
`PReach.toI`, on every library-reachable state under the guarantee of §57. This is not the
contract's statement: `PoolInv` is false on such a state (`Witness.pool_inv_preserved_false`). -/
theorem pool_inv_preserved_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : PoolInvSamePool k L :=
  have ⟨_, hwf, hns, _⟩ := pReachI_inv h
  ⟨entriesDisjoint_of hwf, hns, freeGuaranteeSamePool_of hwf⟩

/-- `pool_entries_disjoint` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 1; §40). -/
theorem pool_entries_disjoint {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    EntriesDisjoint L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).1

/-- `pool_no_stale_access` (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 2): on every state of a library run
(`PReachI`), an active entry authority designates a live slot at its current generation (§89). -/
theorem pool_no_stale_access {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState} (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    NoStale L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.1

/-- `pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.4, item 3):
on every state of a library run (`PReachI`), `freeSlot` never succeeds while the companion of a
resolution of the pool, or an active descendant of it, covers the slot (§43, §69). This is not the
contract's statement: `FreeGuarantee` is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_false`). -/
theorem pool_freeSlot_no_companion_desc_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) : FreeGuaranteeSamePool k L :=
  (pool_inv_preserved_same_pool h).2.2

/-- Exclusivity of a `Modify` companion, as the contract states it (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2:
"Une compagne `Modify` active bloque les nouvelles compagnes sur l'intégralité du stockage du pool";
non-normative library contract): an active `Modify` companion of a pool is the only active
companion that covers a leaf of that pool's storage (§43, §50). The contract does not restrict the
other companions to the same pool. This property is false on a library-reachable state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
def ModifyExclusive (L : PState) : Prop :=
  ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, ∀ pl ∈ L.pools, r₁.pool = pl.id → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
    L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify →
    (∃ l ∈ L.kern.afp r₂.comp, l ∈ footprint L.kern.P pl.storage) → r₁.comp = r₂.comp

/-- `pool_resolve_modify_exclusive`, same-pool restriction (HandlePool v0.4 annex, D.2: "La
propriété d'exclusivité concerne toutes les suites d'opérations admises du noyau"): on every state
of a library run (`PReachI`), whatever its kernel steps, an active `Modify` companion of a pool is
the only active companion of that pool (§43, §50). This is not the contract's statement:
`ModifyExclusive`, which also covers the companions of other pools, is false on such a state
(`Witness.pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_false`). -/
theorem pool_resolve_modify_exclusive_same_pool {k : K} {statics : Statics} {L : PState}
    (h : PReachI k statics L) :
    ∀ r₁ ∈ L.res, ∀ r₂ ∈ L.res, r₁.pool = r₂.pool → L.kern.Active r₁.comp →
      L.kern.Active r₂.comp → r₁.mode = .modify → r₁.comp = r₂.comp := by
  intro r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp ha₁ ha₂ hm
  refine Decidable.byContradiction fun hne => ?_
  have := (pReachI_inv h).2.2.2 r₁ hr₁ r₂ hr₂ hp hne ha₁ ha₂
  rw [hm] at this; cases this.1

## HP-4 (minor, record only, no code change)

`freeSlot` is a transition outside O1–O16 (`XStep.contentEnd`). On a `PReachI` state whose slot content
is `Init`, `freeSlot` ends that content. Kernel `endUse` is rejected both for the slot place and for the
storage root, and `internal` stays active. The reviewer's evidence is
`FreeNotKernel.free_outside_kernel` in `review2/libs/misc.lean`. The library run's kernel side
therefore leaves kernel `Reachable`.

This conflicts with §36 ("These abstractions remain libraries and add no rights to the kernel") and §89
("do not modify the authority-discipline kernel"). Yet the behaviour is prescribed by D.3 (the exemption
----
  - `newPool` = none
  - `allocSlot` = one `write` by an authority found by `writer`
- `freeSlot` is not a kernel step. Its kernel part is `endUseEff` under `ContentEndPre`, which is `HandlePool.XStep.contentEnd`. So a run's kernel state is in `HandlePool.XReach`. It is `Reachable` exactly when the run has no `freeSlot`.
